warnings.message: SCOPe levels above superfamily do not imply homology.

item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q026_protein_kinase_like_function_transfer","answer":"SCOPe 2.08 places these catalytic domains in class d, Alpha and beta proteins (a+b), fold d.144, Protein kinase-like (PK-like), and superfamily d.144.1, Protein kinase-like (PK-like). The three named activities are separate families inside that one superfamily: phosphoinositide 3-kinase catalytic domains are d.144.1.4, SUNID 56171; aminoglycoside phosphotransferases are APH phosphotransferases, d.144.1.6, SUNID 64411; and canonical protein-kinase catalytic subunits are d.144.1.7, SUNID 88854. The justified evolutionary statement is therefore a superfamily-level one: the catalytic cores are inferred to be homologous in SCOPe, not merely similar at the fold level. The justified mechanistic transfer is only the broad protein-kinase-like ATP-dependent phosphoryl-transfer scaffold and any individual catalytic residues whose equivalence is established by alignment or structure. It is unsafe to transfer the family-specific acceptor substrate from one family to another: canonical kinases phosphorylate protein Ser/Thr/Tyr sites, APH enzymes phosphorylate aminoglycoside small molecules, and PI3Ks phosphorylate phosphoinositide lipids. A PI3K or APH fold match is also not enough to assign protein-kinase activation-loop control, eukaryotic regulatory-domain control, lipid binding, aminoglycoside resistance, inhibitor selectivity, exact domain boundaries, or a particular Ser/Thr/Tyr specificity. Those claims require external evidence at the appropriate level, for example direct biochemical substrate and kinetic assays, mutagenesis of the proposed catalytic and specificity residues, a structure or high-confidence model covering the substrate/regulatory interface, and sequence/phylogenetic placement showing conservation of the motifs that make that interface and regulation work. Templates should be chosen from the same SCOPe family or a closer experimentally characterized subfamily whenever the modeled property is a specificity pocket, regulatory loop, or insert; more distant d.144.1 representatives are useful mainly for the conserved bilobal kinase-like core.","evidence_used":["mcp__scope.get_scop_node /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/56111","mcp__scope.get_scop_node /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/56111/parents","mcp__scope.get_scop_node /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/56111/homology","mcp__scope.get_scop_node /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/56112","mcp__scope.get_scop_node /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/56112/parents","mcp__scope.get_scop_node /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/56112/homology","mcp__scope.get_scop_node /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/56171","mcp__scope.get_scop_node /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/64411","mcp__scope.get_scop_node /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/88854","mcp__scope.list_scop_children /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/d.144.1/children"]}]}
